newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Libyan, Moroccan prime ministers seek to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Libyan, Moroccan prime ministers seek to boost ties.

text.p: The Libyan and Moroccan prime ministers on Saturday held talks in Rabat during which they pledged to boost cooperation.

The official Moroccan news agency MAP said visiting Prime Minister Abdelmajid al-Gu'ud said both countries would increase trade and encourage joint investments and cooperation in economic and other vital areas.
Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali said he was convinced that ties between the two peoples "incite us to redouble efforts to extend bilateral cooperation to all fields."
They should intensify trade, develop investment to realise economic projects in the interests of both countries, MAP quoted him as saying.
He also called for an examination of ways that could boost links in teaching, culture, information, health, tourism and professional training.
Gu'ud, secretary of Libya's General Popular Committee, called for the two countries to hold a meeting of their joint commission in March in Tripoli to draw up new strategic programmes.
MAP said that Gu'ud, who arrived late on Friday and was expected to leave Morocco on Saturday, also carried greetings to King Hassan from Libyan leader Colonel Muammar Gaddafi.
